items.summary: Run fp32 element-read linear-texture probe on gfx1100 (Linux) and gfx1201 (Windows): build+run projects/TIGRE/probe/tex_filter_probe.cpp, record verdict (REJECTED/LINEAR/POINT) in probe/README.md table. Baseline gfx90a=REJECTED. Lets us scope the TIGRE PR texture claim and PORTING_GUIDE arch-scope precisely.

When moat-port syncs CERN/TIGRE#809 (multi-GPU TV halo exchange overlap), the fork's cuda_to_hip.h needs four new mappings the PR's commits use in GD_TV.cu, GD_AwTV.cu and tv_proximal.cu: cudaEventCreateWithFlags, cudaEventDisableTiming, cudaStreamWaitEvent and cudaMemcpyPeerAsync (to their hip* names). Since commit f7ef26a, cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer, cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess and cudaErrorPeerAccessAlreadyEnabled appear only in gpuUtils.cu's CUDA-only branch and need no mapping. The MI355X/gfx942 validation of #809 added the mappings only in never-pushed scratch branches, so without them the HIP build of the synced fork fails to compile. Nothing to do until #809 merges upstream and a sync round starts.

items.summary: Upstream fragility, not a port defect: in kernelPixelDetector_parallel_interpolated (ray_interpolated_projection_parallel.cu, same on CUDA) the parallel-beam ray length |S-P| is exactly 2*DSO/dVoxel (128 for the 64^3 test geometry), an exact multiple of accuracy 0.5, so ceilf(length/accuracy) sits on a knife edge between 256 and 257 samples and a 1-ulp change in the float32 squared norm flips it. Which side a build lands on is decided by the compiler's FMA contraction of dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz: CDNA (gfx90a, gfx942) pairs the squares into v_pk_mul_f32 and rounds both, giving 257 samples on 768 of 4096 rays at angle 0.3 and 256 at 0.3+2pi, so test_forward_is_invariant_to_a_full_turn[parallel-interpolated] fails (2.40e-4 vs 1e-4) on MI250X; RDNA (gfx1100, gfx1201) forms an fma chain and gets 256 everywhere. A strict-IEEE CPU emulation agrees with gfx90a/gfx942. A maintainer running the suite on MI250X sees the failure. Options for a person: report upstream with a suggested fix (e.g. a small tolerance before the ceilf, or computing the parallel ray length analytically), or leave it. Whether nvcc lands on the failing side is unverified.
